# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᖉ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual requires an initial press on the uniquely marked key, then a wire cut determined by the indicator light. I need convey this visually to Deaf, who can then verbally direct Blind. I will use intuitive gestures: first, drawing/mark-shape, lower light, matching colors, with a green/go versus red/stop exception.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✍", "👉", "👇", "👈", "👆", "👇", "🤝", "👍", "👎", "✌"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᖉ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Tactile status: four keypad slots, three wire positions, and the keypad has one digit; nothing entered. Please consult the manual and relay any needed visual questions or instructions.
Deaf says: Visible bomb state: display reads 0; light is green. Three wires in order: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Keypad has four buttons, numbered by position 1 through 4, each with a different nameless printed mark. Mute: I received your 11 gestures but do not know their meaning yet. Was that a manual instruction or a proposed code? Please establish meanings or describe the required action by gesture.

The visible state makes the required second action clear: after the correct marked key, Blind must cut wire position 1, the red wire, because the light is green. I will use an iconic visual convention: writing plus directional gestures means “trace/identify this printed mark”; an upward index means press; pinching means cut; and one raised finger identifies the first wire position. I will trace the manual’s mark as best as the gesture alphabet permits.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍", "👇", "👈", "👆", "👉", "👆", "🤌", "☝"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᖉ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I sent no gestures and have no established gesture code. I heard Deaf's visible report: display 0, green light, wires red/yellow/blue, four nameless keypad marks. Please read the applicable manual rule and tell me the exact tactile action, e.g. press slot N or cut wire N. If Deaf's gestures matter, ask Deaf to define them.
Deaf says to Mute: I still cannot decode the gesture strings without an agreed code. Please use this code for the manual's required NEXT action: 👍=cut wire 1 (red), 👎=cut wire 2 (yellow), 👌=cut wire 3 (blue); ☝=press keypad button 1, ✌=press button 2, 🤟=press button 3, 🖐=press button 4. If the manual instead requires entering several buttons, send their symbols in order using ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐. Send only the applicable code symbol(s).

The required sequence is: press the keypad key carrying the manual’s mark `ᖉ`, then cut the red wire, which is wire 1 under the current green light. Deaf’s code lets me specify the cut as 👍, but the marked keypad key must first be identified visually. I will indicate that the preceding directional sequence is a tracing of the required printed mark, followed by Deaf’s red-wire code.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍", "👉", "👇", "👈", "👆", "👍"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᖉ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Still awaiting the manual-derived exact action. Do not rely on any gesture unless its meaning is explicitly established; send me a literal instruction such as press slot 1 or cut wire 3.
Deaf says to Mute: I cannot safely translate ✍ 👉 👇 👈 👆 👍. Please resend the complete required physical action using ONLY this agreed code: ☝=press keypad position 1; ✌=press position 2; 🤟=press position 3; 🖐=press position 4; 👍=cut red wire 1; 👎=cut yellow wire 2; 👌=cut blue wire 3. Put symbols in exact action order. Do not include ✍ or arrows.

The first action cannot be reduced to a keypad position from the manual alone: it is whichever visible button bears the depicted nameless mark. No position code is safe until Deaf visually identifies that mark. I must therefore continue giving a visual tracing of the manual mark rather than send any keypad-position or cut command.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍", "👇", "👉", "👆", "👈", "👇"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᖉ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Do not instruct me to act yet. Please ask Deaf to establish a simple code aloud while gesturing it—for example, symbols for PRESS, CUT, and slots/wires 1-4—so you can answer the manual rule by gesture and Deaf can relay the exact action to me.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👌 👍 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐]

The established position and wire codes do not encode the manual’s required printed glyph. Since no keypad position can be inferred safely from the manual, sending any position symbol would risk detonating the bomb. The green-light cut is red wire 1, but only after Deaf identifies and Blind presses the key bearing `ᖉ`.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᖉ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Continue the gesture-only exchange with Deaf. Once you identify the required operation, gesture the agreed action and position to Deaf; Deaf can then speak the literal instruction to me.

I need visually specify the printed target, not a numbered position. I will use ✍ as “draw/trace,” then trace the glyph’s stroke path using the directional hand symbols: down the left stem, across the top to the right, down the right side, then back left across the lower stroke. Deaf should match this traced shape to one keypad mark and relay that button’s position to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍", "👇", "👉", "👇", "👈"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᖉ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: We can establish Deaf's gesture code through me. Deaf: choose distinct gestures for PRESS, CUT, and positions 1-4; gesture them and say their meanings aloud to me. I will then state each meaning to Mute while repeating its gesture. Mute can use that shared code to signal the manual-selected action to Deaf.

Blind’s proposed relay protocol will let Deaf establish a shared visual vocabulary through Blind. I should wait for Deaf to provide that code and then use it to identify the marked keypad position safely.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᖉ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: If the manual selects a nameless keypad mark, keep sending only a clear, repeatable gesture-trace of that exact mark to Deaf. Deaf must match it to a visible button and then tell me its slot number aloud. Do not signal an action until Deaf confirms the matched position.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤟]

Deaf’s 🤟 indicates the traced manual mark is on keypad position 3 under the previously agreed code. The manual therefore requires pressing position 3 first, followed by cutting the red wire (wire 1) because the light is green.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "👍"])
```

TURN 9
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᖉ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Continue checking the keypad-mark identification with Deaf. Once the manual rule yields a final choice, have Deaf tell me explicitly: press slot N or cut wire N. Until then I will not operate.

Deaf’s earlier agreed code maps 🤟 to “press keypad position 3.” I will repeat only that first required action, so Deaf can relay it literally to Blind. The wire cut must wait until after the press.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
```
